title: Jointly private linear bandits with independent contexts and a uniform positive gap
summary: Each round reveals a context or action-feature set before the learner chooses an action and observes its reward with linear conditional mean. The algorithm must satisfy joint differential privacy: one user's information has limited influence on actions shown to other users. Contexts are i.i.d. from an unknown distribution. All suboptimal actions have a common positive gap lower bound.

model.instance: Contexts $x_t$ are sampled independently from an unknown distribution $P$. The finite action set $\mathcal A$ and feature map $\phi$ are public. The fixed unknown parameter and features lie in the Euclidean unit ball: $$\|\phi(x,a)\|_2\le1,\quad\|\theta_\star\|_2\le1,\quad Y_t\in[-1,1],\quad\mathbb E[Y_t\mid x_t,a_t,\mathcal H_{t-1}]=\langle\phi(x_t,a_t),\theta_\star\rangle.$$ Rewards are fresh draws from the current conditional distribution. The context is observed before choosing an action; its reward is revealed afterwards. Define $f^\star(x,a)=\langle\phi(x,a),\theta_\star\rangle$. Optimal actions may tie, but every suboptimal action has the same uniform positive-gap lower bound: $$a\notin\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in\mathcal A}f^\star(x,b)\ \Longrightarrow\ \max_{b\in\mathcal A}f^\star(x,b)-f^\star(x,a)\ge\Delta_{\min}>0.$$

restrictions: Neighboring streams $\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{\prime}$ differ only in one user's context/reward pair. The protected output is every action except that user's current recommendation, received privately. For every measurable event $E$, require:
$$\Pr\!\left(\mathcal M(\mathsf D)_{-t}\in E\right)\le e^{\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}}\Pr\!\left(\mathcal M(\mathsf D^{\prime})_{-t}\in E\right)+\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}.$$
The privacy relaxation constrains the entire output mechanism. Performance is measured in expectation, without a separate external statistical failure probability.
